text: 🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico is a free, independent and sovereign country. Sovereignty means the people rule — not a foreign power." In La Paz, Sheinbaum placed national sovereignty at the center of her second-year report: "No foreign power, no elite, defines the future of the nation. That is the independence of Mexico." — Claudia Sheinbaum — Honestidad y Resultados, Baja California Sur

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Diesel tax held at zero to shield prices from an oil spike</u>

For a second straight week Hacienda is holding the diesel IEPS at zero — a 100% stimulus worth 7.36 pesos a liter — and widened the Magna break to 4.20 and Premium to 3.34 pesos, a fiscal shield costing 393–481 million pesos a day, per El Economista. The move answers a 9%-plus jump in world oil prices from Middle East tensions, keeping fuel from feeding into transport, food and inflation.

🏠🇲🇽 <u>667,000 Bienestar homes under contract</u>

Mexico's Vivienda para el Bienestar program now has 667,000 homes under contract across 766 projects — 277,000 already under construction — backed by 75.9 billion pesos, hitting 37% of the six-year goal of 1.8 million units aimed at 12 million families. Sedatu puts the investment near 1.2% of GDP a year, generating about four jobs per home — a public housing build-out at a scale the market never delivered.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Huachicol-fiscal probe reaches Navy-linked networks</u>

As the huachicol fiscal investigation reaches Navy-linked networks — the detained Farías Laguna brothers, relatives of former Marina secretary Adm. Rafael Ojeda — Sheinbaum stated there is "ninguna carpeta de investigación contra el almirante Ojeda," who was only asked to testify at a defendant's request. The 4T's crackdown on the fuel-theft-and-tax-fraud rings now reaches into the institutions themselves.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>'Any pretext for intervention must be rejected'</u>

A survey making the rounds claims most Mexicans would welcome foreign intervention against organized crime. Sheinbaum's answer: it "no tiene nada de realidad, nada, porque ni siquiera se dice la fuente" — no source, no reality — and "cualquier pretexto para injerencia o intervención debe ser rechazado, porque viola nuestra soberanía." Cooperation is fine, she said, but the decisions belong to the Mexican people.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US 'safe third country' deals are deportee trafficking</u>

Migration scholar Jorge Durand, writing in La Jornada, calls the US "safe third country" deals what they are — trafficking in deportees: Washington pressures poorer states to warehouse the people it expels, and 13 Latin American and Caribbean countries now take migrants who aren't their own — "México el primero," ahead of Costa Rica, Panama and El Salvador. Others ship the deported as far as South Sudan, Rwanda and Eswatini, whose leaders accept them for a few tens of millions of dollars.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>15 years in prison for defending his forest</u>

In Oaxaca, Zapotec campesino Pablo López Alavez lost 15 years to prison on a "qualified homicide" charge invented to punish him for defending his community's forest — seized in 2010 by 15 hooded men without a warrant, sentenced in 2017 to 30 years, and freed only in 2026 when the fabricated case finally collapsed. La Jornada counts him among the environmental defenders criminalized for standing between the forest and the loggers.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>76% OF MEXICO’S CARS GO NORTH</u>

Mexico built 344,940 vehicles in August and exported 300,475 — with the US absorbing 76.3% of this year’s auto exports, some 1.7 million units, per INEGI/AMIA data. Output slipped 1.4%, the fourth monthly dip of 2026, yet domestic sales hit their highest January-August level since records began in 2005.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>PUBLIC OFFICE, ONE NATIONALITY</u>

Building on Sheinbaum’s sovereignty agenda, Senator Laura Escalante of Oaxaca has introduced an initiative to require Senate candidates to hold Mexican nationality only — extending a rule already in force for the presidency, governors and mayors. “Regardless of the office, public servants must answer solely to the interests of the homeland,” the proposal reads, citing past governors accused of serving foreign interference.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>WHEN THE REAL NARCO-STATE GOT A PASS</u>

A 2013 US State Department report documented 26,121 people disappeared under Calderón (2006-2012), 7,000 unidentified bodies, and systematic torture by security forces — yet Obama imposed zero sanctions and never said “narco-government,” keeping the Mérida money flowing. Calderón’s security chief, García Luna, was later convicted in a US court of taking millions in cartel bribes while running the drug war.
